clinician.final_diagnosis: COVID-19 diagnosed through an imaging study of the retina
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old healthy anesthetist developed sudden temporal relative scotoma in the left eye with normal visual acuity and unremarkable fundus examination. Swept-source OCT imaging revealed a hyperreflective band at the ganglion cell and inner plexiform layers sparing the outer retina, indicating subtle retinal involvement possibly related to COVID-19. The patient had exposure to COVID-19 patients in the prior 5 weeks. RT-PCR testing for SARS-CoV-2 was negative. Serological testing was ordered but results were not documented. Despite lack of positive laboratory confirmation, the retinal OCT findings in the clinical context of significant COVID-19 exposure support the diagnosis of COVID-19 retinal involvement.
